info.title: API Overview
info.description:
Use this API to automate Textverified workflows and integrate your applications.

If you use Python, our official Python client can help you get started faster.

For a high-level summary of how to create a verification or rental, see Purchase Flows.

To test without using account balance, start with Testing with Mock Responses, then use the Postman Mock Collection for runnable requests.

You can also try requests from these docs. Create a bearer token, set it in Authentication, then open the endpoint you want to call.

Purchase Flows

These flows show the recommended request order for creating verifications and rentals.

Verification Flow

Use this flow for single-use of numbers.

  1. Authenticate: Authentication
  2. Choose a verification service: Service List
  3. Optional: check verification pricing or inventory before purchase.
  4. Create a verification: Create Verification
  5. Follow the returned Location header to get verification details.

Rental Flow

Use this flow for long-term use of numbers.

  1. Authenticate: Authentication
  2. Choose a rental service: Service List
  3. Optional: check rental pricing or inventory before purchase.
  4. Create a rental: Create New Rental
  5. Follow the returned Location header to get sale details.
  6. Use the sale response to open the rental details. If the sale includes a backorder, follow that link to track it.

Follow Links

We recommend using returned links and Location headers for follow-up requests instead of constructing URLs manually. Each link includes the href and method to use next.

  • After a successful create request, follow the returned Location header for the next request.
  • Treat the Location header as the URL to follow; parsing IDs from it is unnecessary.
  • Verification create responses return a verification details link. Fetch the verification to see its current status and follow-up links.
  • Rental create responses return a sale details link. Fetch the sale to find the created rental and related links.
  • Paginated responses include next and previous links. See Paginated List Responses for details.
  • Mock responses use the same link pattern as live responses.

Paginated List Responses

Paginated endpoints return results in pages. The response includes a links object with current, previous, and next values. Each link contains an href and method.

To get more results, follow links.next. To move backward, follow links.previous. If a link is missing, there are no more results in that direction.

Example

After calling List SMS, fetch the next page like this:

  • Read href = data['links']['next']['href']
  • Read method = data['links']['next']['method']
  • Fetch the next page: nextPage = fetch(href, { method })
  • Repeat until links.next is missing.

Rate Limits and Retries

The API may return 429 Too Many Requests for authentication, service list, pricing, inventory, and reservation-changing requests. Limits may change, so integrations should be able to handle throttling gracefully.

As a safe default, reuse bearer tokens until they expire, cache stable lookup data, keep request rates steady, and send reservation-changing requests one at a time per account when possible.

Best Practices

  • Cache bearer tokens. Refresh a token only when it is close to expiring.
  • For service list, pricing, and inventory, keep requests steady and cache stable lookup data. After a 429, wait and retry with exponential backoff and jitter.
  • Send reservation-changing requests one at a time per account when possible. For concurrent creates, use a different Idempotency-Key for each purchase.
  • Retry temporary network errors and 5xx responses with a retry limit and exponential backoff. After a create timeout, retry with the same Idempotency-Key if one was supplied. Otherwise check if a sale or reservation was created before you retry.

Safe Retries for Create Requests

Create Verification and Create New Rental support an optional Idempotency-Key header. Use a new key for each purchase. Keys are trimmed and must be 1 to 256 characters.

  • If a create request times out, retry with the same key.
  • If the first request completed, the retry returns the same 201 response.
  • If the first request is still running, the retry returns 409 Conflict with error code IdempotencyConflict; wait and retry with the same key.
  • If the first request expired without completing, the retry returns 400 Bad Request; start a new purchase with a new key.
  • Do not reuse a key for another purchase or reservation type.
  • Without this header, create requests behave as before and should not be retried after an unclear timeout.

Testing with Mock Responses

Use the documented test_* service names with pricing, inventory, and create endpoints.

Use mock_* IDs when reading mock resources or following returned links.

Create responses use the same Location header and link shape as live responses, so follow the returned Location header and response links.

For runnable requests, use the Postman Mock Collection.

Mock service names are documented here rather than returned by Service List. Mock resources are fixed test data and do not appear in account history.

Supported mock responses include X-Phoneblur-Mock: true, which can help you identify mock traffic in tests and logs.

Mock Limits

  • Mock requests do not create real phone numbers or billing events.
  • Mock create requests validate Idempotency-Key when sent, but mock responses are fixed test data and do not store idempotency state.
  • Mock action responses are not persisted. For example, when a supported mock action returns success, later GET responses still show the original mock data.
  • Mock pricing and inventory return fixed values regardless of duration, area code, carrier, or other options. Live responses may vary by those options.
  • Mock resources are available only on endpoints that document mock support. Endpoints that do not document mock support return normal account data.
  • To inspect final states, use fixed mock IDs such as mock_ver_cancelled, mock_ver_reported, mock_ver_reused, or mock_bo_fulfilled. Use mock_bc_paginated to test paginated rental links.

How To Use It

  1. Authenticate normally.
  2. Use one of the listed test_* values in pricing, inventory, or create requests.
  3. Follow the returned Location header and response links the same way you would with live account data.
  4. Use X-Phoneblur-Mock when present to identify mock traffic in tests or logs.

Verification Scenarios

Use these values as serviceName when calling Create Verification.

InputCreate ResultUse For
test_success201 verification details linkCompleted verification, SMS code 123456, and successful reuse within the 30-second reuse window.
test_delayed_success201 verification details linkPending verification that completes after about 30 seconds. You can poll verification details or SMS, but webhooks are recommended for production integrations.
test_pending201 verification details linkPending verification with empty SMS results and cancel/report links.
test_reactivatable201 verification details linkCompleted verification with an expired reuse window and a reactivate link.
test_timeout201 verification details linkTimed-out verification with empty SMS results.

For create-error cases, see the Mock Error Matrix.

Rental Scenarios

Use these values as serviceName when calling Create New Rental.

InputCreate ResultUse For
test_success201 sale linkSuccessful renewable or non-renewable rental. Fetch the sale to find the rental ID.
test_renewable_expired201 sale linkRenewable expired rental. Requires isRenewable=true. Use the returned rental ID to test rental reactivation.
test_nonrenewable_expired201 sale linkNon-renewable expired rental. Requires isRenewable=false. Use the returned rental ID to test rental reactivation.
test_backorder201 sale link when allowBackOrderReservations=trueBackorder flow. Use mock_bo_fulfilled directly to test a fulfilled backorder.

For create-error cases, see the Mock Error Matrix.

Mock IDs

Use these fixed IDs when you want to call a mock details or follow-up endpoint directly. For create requests, prefer following the returned Location header and response links.

Delayed verification responses generate timestamped IDs such as mock_ver_delay_*; use the returned Location header for those.

Rental examples use 30d; other supported rental duration suffixes are 1d, 3d, 7d, 14d, 90d, and 1y.

Postman Mock Collection

Download the Postman collection for mock test cases to run the documented mock flows.

  1. Import the collection into Postman.
  2. Set apiUsername, apiKey, and baseUrl if needed.
  3. Run Generate Bearer Token.
  4. Run the pricing/inventory, verification, and rental folders you want to test.

The collection checks expected response statuses and stores returned IDs and links as collection variables for later requests.

post.description: Generate a bearer token to start making requests to secured endpoints. You will need to supply the following headers: 1) ```X-API-KEY``` (your primary API key) 2) ```X-API-USERNAME``` (your username, which is the email you used to register) All secured endpoints will need your bearer token supplied to them. Because bearer tokens can expire due to having a limited lifespan, you will need to obtain a new bearer token by generating a new one periodically. You can view and manage your API keys under API Settings. After successfully generating a bearer token ```eyJh...```, you can set the bearer token here and explore our secured API endpoints.

get.description: Retrieves the details of the currently authenticated account. Returns the username and current balance (in account credits) of the user, or ``` 401 Unauthorized ``` if the user is not authenticated.

Returns a list of supported area codes.

Use returned ```areaCode``` values in requests that accept an ```areaCodeSelectOption``` body or query parameter.

Returns a list of supported services. These service names are used in API calls that accept a ```serviceName``` value. Mock service names are intentionally not returned here. See Testing with Mock Responses for supported ```test_*``` values.

post.description: Get available rental inventory quantity for a specific service and option(s). Supported services can be found at Service List. Not all services and options are compatible with each other. This endpoint will return a ```400 Bad Request``` for unsupported service and option combinations. The returned ```availableQuantity``` is capped at ```9000```. A value of ```9000``` means ```9000 or more``` are available. Supports documented mock service names. See Testing with Mock Responses for supported ```test_*``` values and behavior.

Get available verification inventory quantity for a specific service and option(s). Supported services can be found at Service List. Not all services and options are compatible with each other. This endpoint will return a ```400 Bad Request``` for unsupported service and option combinations. The returned ```availableQuantity``` is capped at ```9000```. A value of ```9000``` means ```9000 or more``` are available. Supports documented mock service names. See Testing with Mock Responses for supported ```test_*``` values and behavior.

Get rental prices for a specific service and option(s). Supported services can be found at Service List. Not all services and options are compatible with each other. This endpoint will return a ```400 Bad Request``` for unsupported service and option combinations. Supports documented mock service names. See Testing with Mock Responses for supported ```test_*``` values and behavior.

Get verification prices for a specific service and option(s). Supported services can be found at Service List. Not all services and options are compatible with each other. This endpoint will return a ```400 Bad Request``` for unsupported service and option combinations. Supports documented mock service names. See Testing with Mock Responses for supported ```test_*``` values and behavior.

get.description: Get the details on a reservation sale by ID. Supports documented mock sale IDs. See Testing with Mock Responses for supported ```mock_*``` values and behavior.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID of the sale. If the sale ID does not exist, a 404 response will be returned.

get.description: Get a list of your reservation sales. This endpoint is paginated. See Paginated List Responses for details.

Get the details of a billing cycle by ID. A billing cycle can have one or many renewable rentals. Only renewable rentals are associated with a billing cycle. Supports documented mock billing cycle IDs. See Testing with Mock Responses for supported ```mock_*``` values and behavior.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID of the billing cycle. If the billing cycle ID does not exist, a 404 response will be returned.

post.description:
Update a billing cycle by ID.

What you can currently update are:
- ```nickname``` (Your custom string to identify the billing cycle)
- ```remindersEnabled``` (Email reminders)

Not providing an update option will leave it unchanged. For example, not providing ```remindersEnabled``` but having 
```"nickname": "aNickname"``` will only update the nickname.

get.description: Get the invoice history of a billing cycle by its ID. This endpoint is paginated. See Paginated List Responses for details. Supports documented mock billing cycle IDs. See Testing with Mock Responses for supported ```mock_*``` values and behavior.

Returns a list of your billing cycles. A billing cycle can have one or many renewable rentals. Only renewable rentals are associated with a billing cycle. This endpoint is paginated. See Paginated List Responses for details.

post.description: Get an invoice preview for your next billing cycle by its ID.
Renew the active rentals on your billing cycle by its ID. This does not renew overdue rentals. Renew overdue rentals separately with the Renew Overdue Rental endpoint.

get.description: Get the details on a back order reservation by ID. Back order reservations can be created when ```allowBackOrderReservations``` is ```true``` on a new rental request and there is no available stock. See Create New Rental for more info. Supports documented mock backorder IDs. See Testing with Mock Responses for supported ```mock_*``` values and behavior.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID of the back order reservation. If the reservation ID does not exist, a 404 response will be returned.

get.description: Get the details of a line reservation by ID. Supports documented mock IDs. See Testing with Mock Responses for supported ```mock_*``` values and behavior.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID of the line reservation. If the reservation ID does not exist, a 404 response will be returned.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Type of line reservation. If the type supplied does not match the reservation, a 404 response will be returned.

get.description: Gets the health of a reservation and its line number.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID of the line reservation. If the reservation ID does not exist or if the reservation is not 'active', a 404 response will be returned.

post.description: Create/purchase a new verification. Supported services can be found at Service List. If successful, the API returns 201 with a verification details link. Follow the returned ```Location``` header to get verification details. Some combinations of options are unavailable. Will return ```400 Bad Request``` if the request is invalid. To validate without the risk of using credits, use the verification pricing endpoint. Optional retry safety: send ```Idempotency-Key``` with a unique value for each verification purchase. Keys are trimmed and must be 1 to 256 characters. If the request times out, retry with the same key. A completed purchase returns the same 201 verification link. A purchase that is still running returns ```409 Conflict``` with error code ```IdempotencyConflict```; wait and retry with the same key. A purchase that expired without completing returns ```400 Bad Request```; start a new purchase with a new key. Requests without this header are unchanged and should not be retried after an unclear timeout. Supports documented mock service names. See Testing with Mock Responses for supported ```test_*``` values and behavior.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Optional unique key for safely retrying this verification purchase.

get.description: Returns a list of current verifications. This endpoint is paginated. See Paginated List Responses for details.

Retrieves the details of a verification. Also returns actions that can be performed on the verification, including the ability to cancel, report, reactivate, or reuse the verification. Supports documented mock verification IDs. See Testing with Mock Responses for supported ```mock_*``` values and behavior.

post.description: Call this to attempt to cancel a verification by ID. Returns ```400 Bad Request``` if the verification does not allow cancellation. Supports documented mock verification IDs. See Testing with Mock Responses for supported ```mock_*``` values and behavior.

Call this to attempt to reactivate a completed verification that can no longer be reused. This may not be possible due to a number of reasons - to check eligibility, use verification details. If successful, the API returns 201 with a verification details link. Follow the returned ```Location``` header to get verification details. If the verification is not eligible for reactivation, a ```400 Bad Request``` will be returned with an error message. Supports documented mock verification IDs. See Testing with Mock Responses for supported ```mock_*``` values and behavior.

Call this to attempt to report a verification by ID for issues such as "number already in use", "verification failed", or "code not received". Returns ```400 Bad Request``` if the verification does not allow reporting. Supports documented mock verification IDs. See Testing with Mock Responses for supported ```mock_*``` values and behavior.

Call this to attempt to reuse a verification by ID. This is usable only shortly after a verification has been completed successfully on this ID. To check eligibility, use verification details. If successful, the API returns 201 with a verification details link. Follow the returned ```Location``` header to get verification details. If the verification is not eligible for reuse, a ```400 Bad Request``` will be returned with an error message. Supports documented mock verification IDs. See Testing with Mock Responses for supported ```mock_*``` values and behavior.

Create/purchase a new rental. Supported services can be found at Service List. If ```allowBackOrderReservations``` is ```true``` in the request body, a rental back order will be created if the requested rental is out of stock. If successful, the API returns 201 with a sale details link. Follow the returned ```Location``` header to get sale details. Some combinations of options are unavailable. Will return ```400 Bad Request``` if the request is invalid. To validate without the risk of using credits, use the rental pricing endpoint. Optional retry safety: send ```Idempotency-Key``` with a unique value for each rental purchase. Keys are trimmed and must be 1 to 256 characters. If the request times out, retry with the same key. A completed purchase returns the same 201 sale link. A purchase that is still running returns ```409 Conflict``` with error code ```IdempotencyConflict```; wait and retry with the same key. A purchase that expired without completing returns ```400 Bad Request```; start a new purchase with a new key. Requests without this header are unchanged and should not be retried after an unclear timeout. Supports documented mock service names. See Testing with Mock Responses for supported ```test_*``` values and behavior.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Optional unique key for safely retrying this rental purchase.

get.description: Get the current cost to reactivate an expired rental. Use this before reactivating the rental because the cost may change over time. If the rental is not eligible for reactivation, a ```400 Bad Request``` will be returned with an error message. Supports documented mock rental IDs. See Testing with Mock Responses for supported ```mock_*``` values and behavior.

post.description: Call this to attempt to reactivate an expired rental. The request must include ```maxPrice```; the API returns ```400 Bad Request``` if the current reactivation cost is greater than ```maxPrice```, the request is invalid, or the rental is not eligible for reactivation. If successful, the API returns 201 with a sale details link. Follow the returned ```Location``` header to get sale details. Supports documented mock rental IDs. See Testing with Mock Responses for supported ```mock_*``` values and behavior.

get.description: Get the user notes of a rental by ID.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID of the line reservation. If the reservation ID does not exist, a 404 response will be returned.

post.description: Returns a list of rental tags for the supplied ```reservationIds```. This is a read-only search operation. You may supply up to 500 ```reservationIds``` per request. Duplicates are ignored and the result order is not guaranteed. This endpoint is paginated. See Paginated List Responses for details.

get.summary: List Rental Billing Cycle Upgrade Options
get.description:
Returns upgrade durations for this rental.

Renewable rentals can move to a longer billing cycle. Non-renewable rentals can move onto a billing cycle.

post.description:
Schedules an upgrade for this rental.

Renewable rentals move to a longer billing cycle. Non-renewable rentals move onto the selected billing cycle duration.

Schedule more than 24 hours before the rental ends or renews. The upgrade runs right before that time.

get.summary: Get Pending Rental Billing Cycle Upgrade
get.description:
Gets the pending upgrade for this rental.

Returns ```404 Not Found``` if the rental is missing or has no pending upgrade.

delete.description:
Cancels a pending upgrade for this rental.

You must cancel more than 24 hours before the rental ends or renews. After that, the upgrade cannot be canceled or undone.

Returns ```404 Not Found``` if the rental or pending upgrade is not found.

parameters.name: jobId
parameters.description: ID of the pending billing cycle upgrade job.

get.description: Get the details of a renewable rental by ID. Also returns links to the billing cycle, SMS, calls, and sale information. Supports documented mock rental IDs. See Testing with Mock Responses for supported ```mock_*``` values and behavior.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID of the line reservation. If the reservation ID does not exist, a 404 response will be returned.

post.description:
Update a renewable rental by ID.

What you can currently update are:
- ```userNotes``` (Notes)
- ```includeForRenewal``` (Include/Exclude rental for renew)
- ```markAllSmsRead``` (Mark SMS as read)
- ```tags``` (Replace or clear tags)

Not providing an update option will leave it unchanged. For example, not providing
```userNotes``` but having ```"includeForRenewal": true``` will only include the rental for renew.

get.description: Returns a list of your renewable rentals. Optional Parameters: - ```billingCycleId``` (Get renewable rentals under this billing cycle ID) To create a new rental, see Create New Rental. This endpoint is paginated. See Paginated List Responses for details. Supports documented mock ```billingCycleId``` values. See Testing with Mock Responses for supported ```mock_*``` values and pagination behavior.

post.description: Call this to attempt to refund a renewable rental by ID. This could fail if the rental is not refundable or the refund period has passed. Will return ```400 Bad Request``` if the request is invalid or refund is not possible.

Renew an overdue rental by its ID. 

Calling this method will automatically include the rental for renewal and perform the renewal. Only overdue rentals may be renewed this way.

get.description: Get the details of a non-renewable rental by ID. Also returns links to SMS, calls, and sale information. Supports documented mock rental IDs. See Testing with Mock Responses for supported ```mock_*``` values and behavior.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID of the line reservation. If the reservation ID does not exist, a 404 response will be returned.

post.description:
Update a non-renewable rental by ID.

What you can currently update are:
- ```userNotes``` (Notes)
- ```markAllSmsRead``` (Mark SMS as read)
- ```tags``` (Replace or clear tags)

Not providing an update option will leave it unchanged. For example, not providing
```userNotes``` but having ```"markAllSmsRead": true``` will only mark all SMS for that rental as read.

get.description: Returns a list of your non-renewable rentals. To create a new rental, see Create New Rental. This endpoint is paginated. See Paginated List Responses for details.

post.description:
Extensions are NOT refundable and cannot be undone.

Attempt to extend the duration of a non-renewable rental by ID.

Call this to attempt to refund a non-renewable rental by ID. This could fail if the rental is not refundable or the refund period has passed. Will return ```400 Bad Request``` if the request is invalid or refund is not possible.

get.description: Returns a list of your latest SMS. Optional Parameters: - ```to``` (A phone number) - ```reservationId``` (The reservation's ID) - ```reservationType``` (The reservation's type) This endpoint is paginated. See Paginated List Responses for details. Supports documented mock reservation IDs. See Testing with Mock Responses for supported ```mock_*``` values and behavior.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: If provided, will filter results to only include SMS sent to the specified number.

parameters.name: reservationId
parameters.description: If provided, will filter results to only include SMS associated with the specified reservation.

parameters.name: reservationType
parameters.description: If provided, will filter results to only include SMS associated with the specified reservation type.

post.description: Attempt to reply to an SMS by ID.
Attempt to send an SMS by reservation ID.

get.description: Call this endpoint to obtain a list of calls associated with your account. This endpoint is paginated. See Paginated List Responses for details. Supports documented mock reservation IDs. Mock call lists return empty results. See Testing with Mock Responses for supported ```mock_*``` values and behavior.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: If provided, will filter results to only include calls made to the specified number.

parameters.name: reservationId
parameters.description: If provided, will filter results to only include calls associated with the specified reservation.

parameters.name: reservationType
parameters.description: If provided, will filter results to only include calls associated with the specified reservation type.

post.description: Call this endpoint to create a call access token. This supports incoming calls only. Call sessions are established by: 1. Creating a voice verification and getting the corresponding reservation ID. 2. Posting to this endpoint to obtain a short-lived Twilio access token associated with the reservation ID. 3. Using the access token with Twilio's integration to handle an incoming call. Warning: This is an advanced integration. Support for custom Twilio client behavior is limited. You are responsible for implementing and troubleshooting the client integration, including connectivity, call acceptance, and call termination.

get.description: Get a wake request by ID. The details of a wake request include: - ```isScheduled``` (Indicates if the wake request has been successfully created and enqueued.) - ```usageWindowStart``` (The datetime when you can start using the reservation.) - ```usageWindowEnd``` (The datetime when you will no longer be able to use the reservation.) Creating a successful wake request will enqueue your request on that line reservation. To see the details of your wake request, see Get Wake Request. If successful, the API returns 201 with a wake request details link. Follow the returned ```Location``` header to get wake request details.

The details of an usage window estimate include: - ```estimatedWindowStart``` (The estimated datetime when you can start using the reservation.) - ```estimatedWindowEnd``` (The estimated datetime when you will no longer be able to use the reservation.) Refer to the ```SCHEMA``` below for more details.

get.description: Returns an array of webhook event names that can be subscribed to, such as ```v2.sms.received``` and ```v2.reservation.created```. You must configure your API Webhook Settings and subscribe to events before webhooks will be sent. The schemas of webhook event payloads are documented below. Webhook payloads contain event data in the ```Data``` property and are sent as HTTP POST requests to the webhook URI configured on your account. Validate the webhook signature on your server. Webhook validation: Each webhook request is signed using HMAC-SHA512 and your webhook secret (`whsec_...`). The signature HTTP header is ```X-Webhook-Signature``` and the header value will be prefixed by the signing algorithm ```HMAC-SHA512=```. The signature after the prefix is Base64 encoded. The process for validating a signature is as follows: 1) Extract the HTTP header with the name ```X-Webhook-Signature```. 2) Remove the prefix ```HMAC-SHA512=``` from the HTTP header value, which is obtained from step 1. This Base64 encoded value will be compared to the HTTP request body hash later. 3) Apply the HMAC-SHA512 hashing algorithm to the HTTP request body to obtain a byte array. 4) Apply Base64 encoding to the byte array (obtained from step 3). 5) Compare the value from step 2 to the value from step 4 and verify that they are the same. Webhooks are automatically retried for a period of time with exponential backoff. After multiple failed webhook send attempts, webhooks may be automatically disabled. If this happens, re-enable webhooks in your API Webhook Settings.
